historia: People were already living at the Oppidum de Hornachuelos, probably the Fornacis mentioned by Ptolemy, in the Copper Age, and the settlement was at its height between the 2nd century BC and the 1st century AD.

The Order of Santiago resettled the town in the 13th century, and it became the seat of an encomienda; the first written mention dates from 1257. According to tradition, the name comes from a great ash tree (fresno) on the banks of the Valdemedel stream.

The old town was rebuilt in the 17th and 18th centuries: whitewashed houses with black iron grilles and Baroque mansions bearing coats of arms. The Town Hall occupies the former convent of Jesús y María, founded by the Poor Clares in 1535.

placa.pie: Plaque on the house where the poet was born, in Calle Larga
placa.texto: The plaque reads: «In this house you see was born the admirable poet Don Juan Meléndez Valdés». Juan Meléndez Valdés (1754-1817), poet and judge of the Enlightenment, was born in this street. The town's bronze bust of him dates from 1985 and is the work of Luis Martínez Giraldo.

Casa de Vargas-Zúñiga.texto: A 17th- and 18th-century town mansion, now the Casa de la Cultura (cultural centre) and library.
Casa de Vargas-Zúñiga.alt: Whitewashed façade of the Casa de la Cultura, with iron grilles and balconies

Oppidum de Hornachuelos.texto: A fortified pre-Roman settlement of about five hectares, with an interpretation centre in the Casa de la Cultura.
Oppidum de Hornachuelos.alt: Remains of stone walls of the settlement among the grass

Los pozos rojos y blancos.texto: The wells around the municipality have their body painted red and their rim painted white.
Los pozos rojos y blancos.alt: A well with a red body and a white rim under its iron arch, in the countryside

Lavadero de lanas.texto: The ruined arches of the old wool-washing site, by the Valdemedel stream.
Lavadero de lanas.alt: Ruined brick arches of the old wool-washing site

Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de Gracia.detalle: Dating from the 13th-14th century and rebuilt in 1745 and 1859. Twin towers, a Baroque altarpiece by Alonso Rodríguez Lucas and a pulpit of Estremoz marble. C/ Iglesia, 2.

Ermita del Cristo de la Misericordia.detalle: 18th century, with a forecourt, a side arcade and a tower. It houses the image of Christ that tradition attributes to Pedro Roldán.

Ermita de la Aurora.detalle: In Calle Meléndez Valdés. It keeps the choir stalls of the Thirteen of the Order of Santiago and Visigothic stones in the doorway.

Ermita del Cristo Viejo.detalle: 16th century, now in ruins, with a dome and a tower topped by an onion-shaped finial.

Ermita de San Juan Macías.detalle: Built in 1985 in the house where the saint was born.

Ermita de San Isidro.detalle: Built in 1998, about 4 km from the town.

Casa natal de Juan Meléndez Valdés.detalle: In Calle Larga, with the plaque in memory of the poet.

Monumento a Meléndez Valdés.detalle: A bronze bust from 1985 by the Badajoz sculptor Luis Martínez Giraldo.

Casa de Vargas-Zúñiga.detalle: A 17th- and 18th-century town mansion with a balcony, a coat of arms with a scallop shell and iron grilles bearing the cross of Santiago. It is now the Casa de la Cultura.

Palacio de Quintanilla.detalle: In Calle Ayuntamiento, with a Baroque façade.

Casa de Bazo.detalle: With a balcony beneath a scallop-shell vault.

Casas de los Olea y de los Grajera.detalle: Corner houses with coats of arms, from the 17th and 18th centuries.

Antiguo convento de Jesús y María.nombre: Former convent of Jesús y María
Antiguo convento de Jesús y María.detalle: A convent of Poor Clares founded in 1535. It is now the Town Hall.

Oppidum de Hornachuelos.detalle: A fortified pre-Roman settlement of about five hectares, excavated between 1986 and 1997. Its interpretation centre is in the Casa de la Cultura.

Pozo de San Juan Macías.detalle: On the Valle Garzón estate, about 4 km away: the site of the saint's first miracle.

Pilar del Caño.detalle: A traditional drinking trough on the outskirts of the town.

Los pozos rojos y blancos.detalle: The wells around the municipality have their body painted red and their rim painted white.

Ruinas del lavadero de lanas.detalle: Brick arches by the Valdemedel stream.

Juan Meléndez Valdés.texto: Poet and judge of the Enlightenment. He was born in Calle Larga.

San Juan Macías.texto: Dominican friar in Lima, canonised in 1975. The house where he was born is now a chapel.

Alonso García Bravo.texto: Master builder for Hernán Cortés: he drew up the first plan of Mexico City.

José María Chacón Pachón.texto: Member of parliament during the First Spanish Republic.
